text:
alex: customer reports burst of 5xx from our quota layer when they exceed free tier. They expect 429s but get 503/504. Happened around 11:03 PDT, request id `req_0a9f2b`.

sara: can you paste a sample curl and the response body they saw? also which region?

alex: us-west-2. sample: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' \
  -H 'x-request-id: req_0a9f2b' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","input":"hi"}'
```
response: 503 from quota-gateway with body `{"error":"quota-service-unavailable"}` and no `retry-after`. Customer says this started after maintenance window.

raj: digging into gateway logs — I'm seeing the gateway making requests to `quota-svc` and getting `upstream response: TLS read timeout` then gateway classifies as 502/503 instead of mapping to 429. Looks like the healthcheck route switched to fallback path that doesn't enforce quota semantics. logs: 
```
[11:03:22] gw: outbound -> quota-svc: GET /v1/check?key=acct123
[11:03:23] quota-svc: upstream read timeout
[11:03:23] gw: route fallback to /quota/internal -> returned 503
```

oncall-bot: paging @jin (infra oncall) :rotating_light:

jin: I'm on it — I see the service mesh routed a portion of traffic to the `quota-internal` host because `quota-cache` pool healthcheck failed after the maintenance. That fallback path hits the auth-cache sync which currently has a 500ms internal timeout; during the spike it exceeded that and bubbled as 503. Repro: from prod VPC run: 
```
curl -s -H 'Host: quota-internal.prod' 'http://10.7.4.23/v1/check?key=acct123' -v
```
response shows `504 gateway timeout` at the mesh layer.

jordan: can we short-circuit to quota-fallback-v2 that returns 429 when quota exceeded? we should not expose 5xx for quota failures. Temporary mitigation: update routing rule so gateway uses `quota-fallback-v2` for traffic pinned to the unhealthy pool.

raj: +1. Also the gateway's error mapping uses a generic map that converts a few upstream error codes to 5xx. We need to add a mapping: upstream-timeout -> 429 for quota check endpoints. I'll open a quick PR to change the mapping for `/v1/check`.

maria: I'll coordinate a hotfix deploy. Pushing route change to envoy config now (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). Patch: 
```
# envoy route snippet
- match: /v1/check
  route: quota-fallback-v2
  rewrite_response_code: on
  upstream_timeout: 1500ms
```

alex: pinging support to update customer with ETA. INC-12345 created.

maria: deployed canary at 11:12, error rate dropped from 6.7% to 0.9% within 3m. Promoted to 100% at 11:18.

jin: root cause summary: healthcheck for `quota-cache` pool marked nodes unhealthy after maintenance; service mesh incorrectly routed those flows to `quota-internal` path which relies on a slow auth-cache sync. The gateway mapping converted the resulting upstream timeouts into 5xx without semantic mapping for quota-check endpoints.

raj: actions: 
- revert misroute (done)
- add error-mapping: upstream-timeout -> 429 for quota endpoints (PR #789)
- increase auth-cache sync timeout and add circuit-breaker on quota-internal calls
- add metric `quota.gateway.resp_class` to distinguish 4xx vs 5xx for quota checks

maria: follow-up runbook items: add an automatic rollback window for route changes during maintenance, add a playbook step for contacting oncall when quota svc returns non-4xx.

alex: updated customer with status and that we've applied hotfix; they asked for postmortem and will verify.

jin: monitoring graph attached to thread (link: https://grafana.internal/boards/QUOTA-504) — will keep an eye for 12h.

sara: thanks team. tagging for postmortem owners: @raj (root cause), @maria (mitigation/deploy), @jin (infra/followup). :thumbsup:

alex: marking resolved for now. will file formal incident report and CC CS. :white_check_mark:
__notes: generated slack thread for incident handling of quota service returning 5xx instead of 4xx; includes logs, commands, mitigation steps, and action items
